As a blind individual the extra features that would seem gimmicky to most people are actually extremely useful. Especially having a headphone that pauses or lowers volume of music when conversations begin. Taking out my phone and attempting to hit pause or trying to figure out which rocker is the volume can be frustrating. The noise cancling  is super important with anxiety which a lot of blind individuals experience due to all the noises around us. So having better ambient noise filtration helps with dangerous situations like crossing streets.

I very nearly bought a set of the new Beats Solo3 Wireless (with the W1 chip) to replace my 3 year old half working original Solo3 Wireless before I saw this video. Thank you. Seriously. These things are amazing, and unless the new Solo3's have improved drastically (in terms of sound) from the original set I have, I definitely made the right choice here. So much more comfortable, actually stick out from my head less (I used to hate over-ear headphones because they usually look way too big on my head, but the Beats actually stick out more), sound amazing, and ANC isn't something I knew I needed until I had it. They even look somehow both cool and understated at the same time. 

About the only way I could see that the Beats would be better is they have about 30% more battery life (apparently). But 30 hours is more than enough.
The “Quick Attention” feature (where you put your hand on the earcup to quiet the music) is not new. The XM3s have it.

I owned these a few months ago and now I have some thoughts. 
I thought these were amazing when I first bought them, couldn't believe how good they sounded. Even in those early days though, sometimes I thought "jee I just wish it was slightly clearer" but because I spent so much on them I just assumed this is about as good as it got and just got used to it.
Then however I found a great youtuber called crinacle and he kinda slagged on them a bit, basically calling them beats and that's when it all started falling apart, what I'd be slightly feelng previous was now perfectly crystalised and it's issues of the bass basically bleeding all the way into the mids was unavoidable for me. So I went out and bought a second hand pair of Beyerdynamic DT 990s and instantly the difference was night and day, the DT 990s just were so much clearer with much more detail and were frankly much better tuned. This was just running out of my phone too, no amp or dac yet (which you can do even though they are the 250ohm version). It got to the point where it dawned on me that I'll never use the sonys again so I sold them and haven't looked back since.
 Now this is all to say that they weren't what I was looking for, I was chasing sound quality not a feature rich HEADSET. Most of the features are ones I can live without but that will be on a person to person basis
